issues.legal_issue: A government employee who becomes a co-owner of qualifying residential premises may maintain a special proceeding to recover possession of those premises.
material_facts: The employee had been ordered to vacate government accommodation because he owned residential premises in his wife's name.
His wife died before the recovery petitions were filed, and he became a co-owner of the premises with their children.
The order requiring him to vacate the government accommodation remained in force.
issues.conclusion: The employee was entitled to maintain the recovery petitions as a co-owner.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29B of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 provides a special procedure for a qualifying government employee to recover premises on the ground in Section 13(1)(ff). Applying Kanta Goel v. B.P. Pathak and Shri Ram Pasricha v. Jagannath, a co-owner is an owner of the entire property along with the other co-owners and may maintain the proceeding.

predicates.special_recovery_proceeding: The claimant brought a special proceeding to recover residential premises on the basis of a government employer's requirement that the claimant vacate government-provided accommodation.
predicates.government_vacate_order_active: The requirement that the claimant vacate the government-provided accommodation remained in force when the recovery proceeding was filed.
predicates.claimant_is_property_cow_owner: The claimant held an ownership share in the premises sought to be recovered.
predicates.co_owner_may_seek_possession: A co-owner may maintain the proceeding to recover possession.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings the specified recovery proceeding, remains subject to the government-vacate requirement, and owns a share of the premises, the claimant may seek possession as a co-owner.

issues.legal_issue: An heir landlord may rely on a notice to vacate served by the deceased landlord before the recovery proceeding was filed, without serving a fresh notice.
material_facts: The wife served the tenants with notices to vacate before her death.
After her death, her husband and children, including the husband as a co-owner, filed the recovery petitions.
The notices had been issued for the purpose of giving the tenants prior intimation of the intended eviction proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The husband, as an heir and co-owner, could rely on the notices served by his wife, and fresh notices were unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(6) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 requires prior notice to the tenant. The Court held that the notice's purpose was to give prior intimation of the intended eviction proceeding and that an heir landlord could avail of the notice issued by the deceased landlord; no fresh notice was required.

predicates.special_statutory_eviction_proceeding: The claimant brought a special statutory proceeding to recover rented premises.
predicates.prior_notice_served_by_deceased_landlord: The landlord served the tenant with notice to vacate before dying.
predicates.claimant_is_heir_landlord: The person pursuing recovery is an heir of the landlord who served the notice.
predicates.prior_notice_remains_effective: The heir landlord may rely on the prior notice without serving a fresh notice.

issues.definition: In a special statutory eviction proceeding, when the deceased landlord served prior notice and an heir pursues recovery, that prior notice remains effective.

issues.legal_issue: A government employee's retirement after filing a qualifying special recovery petition does not defeat the petition.
material_facts: The employee filed the recovery petitions while still in government service and while the requirement to vacate government accommodation remained in force.
He retired during the pendency of the petitions.
issues.conclusion: The employee's subsequent retirement did not defeat the petitions that had been duly filed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29B of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 provides the special recovery procedure for a qualifying government employee. Relying on Nihal Chand v. Kalyan Chand Jain, a case under Section 14A of the Delhi Rent Control Act, the Court held that subsequent retirement does not defeat a petition duly filed while the employee qualified to bring it.

predicates.special_recovery_proceeding: The claimant brought a special proceeding to recover premises based on a requirement to vacate government-provided accommodation.
predicates.claimant_qualified_when_filed: The claimant met the requirements to bring the recovery proceeding when it was filed.
predicates.claimant_retired_after_filing: The claimant retired from government service after filing the recovery proceeding.
predicates.petition_survives_subsequent_retirement: The recovery petition is not defeated by the claimant's subsequent retirement.

issues.definition: A qualifying special recovery petition survives when the claimant met the filing requirements and retired only after filing.
